content.body: Perimeter measures the total distance around a two-dimensional shape. Area measures the region it covers. A garden fence follows a boundary; paving covers a region.

quickCheck.prompt: Which quantity measures how much ground a rectangular garden covers?
quickCheck.explanation: Area. Use the relationship and conditions explained in this block.

content.narration: Perimeter measures the total distance around a two-dimensional shape. Area measures the region it covers. A garden fence follows a boundary; paving covers a region.

content.body: A rectangle has two pairs of equal opposite sides. Name its length and width, and measure both in the same unit before calculating. Both dimensions are perpendicular to one another.

content.narration: A rectangle has two pairs of equal opposite sides. Name its length and width, and measure both in the same unit before calculating. Both dimensions are perpendicular to one another.

content.body: Perimeter uses length units such as centimetres or metres. Area uses square units: one square centimetre is a square with sides one centimetre long. Convert all lengths to a common unit before using a formula.

quickCheck.prompt: Which is an appropriate unit for the area of a tabletop?
quickCheck.explanation: Square centimetres. Use the relationship and conditions explained in this block.

content.narration: Perimeter uses length units such as centimetres or metres. Area uses square units: one square centimetre is a square with sides one centimetre long. Convert all lengths to a common unit before using a formula.

content.body: A rectangle of length l and width w has perimeter 2 times the sum of l and w. Its area is l times w. The first calculation adds boundary lengths; the second counts unit squares in rows and columns.

quickCheck.prompt: Which expression gives a rectangle's perimeter?
quickCheck.explanation: 2 times (length plus width). Use the relationship and conditions explained in this block.

content.narration: A rectangle of length l and width w has perimeter 2 times the sum of l and w. Its area is l times w. The first calculation adds boundary lengths; the second counts unit squares in rows and columns.

content.body: For a rectangle with fixed width, increasing length increases both area and perimeter. Doubling only the length doubles the area, but does not generally double the perimeter because the width is unchanged.

content.narration: For a rectangle with fixed width, increasing length increases both area and perimeter. Doubling only the length doubles the area, but does not generally double the perimeter because the width is unchanged.

blocks.title: An angle is a turn

content.body: An angle describes a turn between two rays meeting at a point. Specify which turn is intended when the same rays bound a smaller angle and a reflex angle. The vertex is the common endpoint.

options: The amount of turn between rays
quickCheck.explanation: The amount of turn between rays. Use the relationship and conditions explained in this block.

content.body: Two rays start at a shared vertex and form an angle. In angle ABC, B names the vertex. Extending either ray changes its drawn length but not the turn between the directions.

quickCheck.prompt: In angle ABC, which letter identifies the vertex?
quickCheck.explanation: B. Use the relationship and conditions explained in this block.

content.narration: Two rays start at a shared vertex and form an angle. In angle ABC, B names the vertex. Extending either ray changes its drawn length but not the turn between the directions.

content.body: A degree is one three-hundred-and-sixtieth of a full turn. A right angle is 90 degrees, a straight angle is 180 degrees and a full turn is 360 degrees. Degrees measure turn, not distance.

quickCheck.prompt: How many degrees are in a full turn?
quickCheck.explanation: 360. Use the relationship and conditions explained in this block.

content.narration: A degree is one three-hundred-and-sixtieth of a full turn. A right angle is 90 degrees, a straight angle is 180 degrees and a full turn is 360 degrees. Degrees measure turn, not distance.

content.body: An acute angle is greater than zero and less than 90 degrees. A right angle is 90 degrees; an obtuse angle is greater than 90 and less than 180 degrees. A straight angle is 180 degrees; a reflex angle is greater than 180 and less than 360 degrees.

quickCheck.prompt: How is a marked angle of 120 degrees classified?
quickCheck.explanation: Obtuse. Use the relationship and conditions explained in this block.

content.narration: An acute angle is greater than zero and less than 90 degrees. A right angle is 90 degrees; an obtuse angle is greater than 90 and less than 180 degrees. A straight angle is 180 degrees; a reflex angle is greater than 180 and less than 360 degrees.

blocks.title: Cross-concept connection
blocks.objective: Derive the convex-polygon interior-angle sum from a triangle partition

content.body: For a convex n-sided polygon, the triangle partition gives interior-angle sum (n minus 2) times 180 degrees. A full exterior turn is a different quantity. For a regular polygon all interior angles are equal; equal side lengths alone do not justify equal angles in a general polygon.

blocks.title: Justification
blocks.objective: Derive the convex-polygon interior-angle sum from a triangle partition

content.body: For a convex n-sided polygon, the triangle partition gives interior-angle sum (n minus 2) times 180 degrees. A full exterior turn is a different quantity. For a regular polygon all interior angles are equal; equal side lengths alone do not justify equal angles in a general polygon.
